games/an-unpublished-game.title: an unpublished game
games/an-unpublished-game.content:
an unpublished game
Warp Gate, 2024-12-31
E taught A, J, and I a 4-player space 4X dice game he learned from its creator at Holden Village. It requires 50 d6s, 10 each in 5 colors, and a plain gridded map. The dice act as planets, spaceships, and settlements/shipyards. Building, moving, discovering planets, and battling all involve d6s rolls.
J trounced me because luck was with him and against me.
The creator told E to adapt it as he wanted. I’d give every player a colony ship to start and eliminate warp gates as dice, which didn’t factor at all in our game. I’d add a bonus to fighters when battling bombers and a bonus to everything when battling colony ships. I don’t know what d6s ships could be. Diplomats? Spies?
Planets
1 = unexplored  (“bump” with a colony ship to explore, then roll for its type)
2 = toxic waste (“bump” with a colony ship to terraform to a 5)
3 = hostile aliens  (“bump” with fighter, bomber, or capital ship to attack, when conquered, planet becomes a 5)
4 = friendly aliens (build a trading post 4 or starport 3, gives +1 action bonus)
5 = habitable planet (settle 5, gives +1 action bonus)
6 = home world (settle 6, gives +2 action bonus)
Ships
1 = capital ship (gives +1 reroll bonus)
2 = bombers (+1 vs capital ships and planets)
3 = fighters
4 = nuke (destroys all orthogonal squares, renders planets as toxic waste)
5 = colony ship
6 = warp gate (can travel between warp gates)
Build ships by declaring what you’re building and rolling a d6. If you roll equal to or less than the ship’s number, you build it successfully. If not, you fail, expending the action. Build one ship per turn at settled homeworlds and habitable planets and at your mother ship, two per turn at starports.
Move ships by rolling a d6. You can then move that ship the amount show on the die. Nukes, however, have a maximum movement of 4 spaces. On a 5 or 6, they detonate.
Attack a ship or planet by “bumping” it. Battle is a simple opposed d6 roll, with modifiers. Attacker can reroll if they have remaining rerolls. Ties trigger rerolls for both players.
Players get 2 actions per turn, plus an 2 additional actions per settled home world and 1 additional action per settled habitable planet and trading post. They also get one reroll per turn, plus an additional reroll per capital ship.

rpgs/Dune-Sunday/Dune-inspired-Campaign-.title: Dune-inspired Campaign Player Handout
rpgs/Dune-Sunday/Dune-inspired-Campaign-.content:
Dune-inspired Campaign Player Handout
Campaign Background
Centuries of prosperity corrupted the Dragon Empire. So when Emperor Elrood IX granted Sir Ravd a single dragon’s egg and *Baron Abulyrd’s* settlement of Sikara, even village children knew: it was a trap. This “reward” for honorable service was an attempt to destroy Sir Ravd and his house for being too popular and too good. Annihilation by giants and orcs and winter, if not assassination. If Sir Ravd’s house survives, it promises to embarrass the venal nobility by its shining example. Sikara also promises great wealth. Mines beneath nearby ruins are the last source of dragongems, necessary for incubating dragons’ eggs and, thus, the linchpin of the alliance between metallic dragons and the Emperor.


Campaigns in this setting
Thursday group: The heroes are youths in Sir Ravd’s settlement of Sikara.
Sunday group: The heroes began at More on Camp Booming Chasm, an orc smuggling den near Sikara.



Sikara is under the first ‘o’ in ‘Colossus.’ See the full Dragon Empire map.
Sikara is in the Frost Range, in the westward shadow of the Northern Colossus, south of the Crystalknife Glacier, some 500 miles north of the imperial capital, Axis.
Travel time from Axis to Sikara…

overland: 32 days (if the dwarves allow passage along the Undermarch and the local mountain passes are clear)
via murkship: 9 days
for the Emperor’s dragon-riding Knights of the Noonday at flank speed: 7 days (if the weather is fair)


Characters


For players new to 13th Age
In 13th Age, level 1 characters are already established adventurers. They’re heroes, not just farmers with swords.
  
  📙 The free [13th Age Quickstart Rules](www.pelgranepress.com/shop/pdfs/13th_Age_Quickstart.zip) are a must read, especially the four pages on “Creating Characters" and "Icons." The former has great examples of One Unique Things.
  
  
  📄 [13th Age Character Sheet](site.pelgranepress.com/files/13thAge_Plain_CharacterSheet.pdf)
  
See the 13th Age core rulebook and 13 True Ways for more. Or the free 13th Age SRD (linked version) has rules without setting info.


Available Races & Classes
Kin: Human, Dwarf, Dragonic, Dark Elf, High Elf, Wood Elf, Forgeborn, Gnome, Half-Elf, Half-Orc, Orc, Halfing, Holy One, Tiefling, Alleykin, Arcanite, Beastblooded, Spiritborn, Unholy One.
Classes: Barbarian, Bard, Chaos Mage, Cleric, Commander, Demonologist, Druid, Fighter, Monk, Necromancer, Occultist, Paladin, Ranger, Rogue, Sorcerer, and Wizard.

💡 Have other ideas? Ask.

One Unique Things & Backgrounds


For players new to 13th Age
An OUT is what sets your character apart from everyone else. It doesn’t grant powers. It’s what makes you special and what makes your life interesting. Backgrounds replace skill lists. They’re bits of your backstory that each grant bonuses to a variety of different skill checks.
You as a player get to shape the world and the campaign through your character’s OUT and backgrounds. The more detail you add, especially to backgrounds, the more hooks you give the GM to tailor adventures to your character.
Expand on the backstory in this handout. Add something completely new. Create connections with other characters and with the world. The GM will ask you to change details that conflict with non-negotiable elements of the campaign. But don’t worry, talking through and refining your ideas will be a big part of our first session.


You could have a background, “former sailor in the Imperial navy,” but like Wade Rockett, this is what I love:

Former sailor on the Imperial frigate Intrepid*, which was sunk in battle against the* Revenant*, flagship of the Lich King’s Pale Fleet under the command of the lich admiral Vertinor*




Read more:  13 Tricks for Better Backgrounds (& One Unique Things)




Icons

☀️ **Heroic Icons**


Great Gold Wyrm (Atreides)
The House of Sir Ravd, the Wyrm’s last Knight of the Golden Order, is fighting for survival against the Crusader’s Baron Abulyrd and his shadow-ally, the Emperor.

Orc Lord (Fremen)
Oppressed but fierce, he hoards the secret of dragongems’ true source and his people’s real strength and purposes.

✴️ **Villainous Icons**


Crusader (Harkonnen)
He fought monsters and became a monster, and his most fervent follower is Baron Abulyrd of Glitterhaegen, who is hellbent on destroying Sir Ravd and the Great Gold Wyrm.

Emperor (Emperor):
Emperor Elrood IX’s military power on land and in air is unmatched, thanks to his fearsome army of Knights of the Dawn and metallic dragon-riding Knights of the Noonday Sun. Baron Abulyrd disgusts him but Sir Ravd is a real threat. So he backs the Baron, if secretly.

Lich King (Tleilaxu)
His followers will bring back anyone…for a price.

Diabolist (Ixian)
She devises the most infernal of machines.

❓ **Ambiguous Icons**


Priestess (Bene Gesserit)
The ubiquitous priestesses of Mother Siona Arrbea Mohmus Chotkoba live to serve so well that no one notices as they finesse history toward their own ends. Hopefully those are benevolent. (There are no male priests, only female priestesses.)

Archmage (Spacing Guild)
Only her wizards can safely slip her barges, called murkships, into and through the Murk. Her monopoly on (relatively) fast, long-range travel and transport earns her wealth, power, and resentment. It also depends on dragongems.

Prince of Shadows (CHOAM)
The black market is THE market, and he controls it. Goods, titles, secrets…but by far, dragongems bring the highest prices.
Elf Queen, High Druid, Dwarf King, The Three (the Landsraad)
These minor icons talk a noble game in support of Sir Ravd, but when push comes to shove, do they really just want wealth and power?





Other Dune connections
Sanganak Gnomes (Mentats)
All Sanganaks are gnomes, not all gnomes are Sanganaks. Sanganaks require regular contact with dragongems to maintain their incredible abilities for weighing possibilities, recalling lore, and seeing to the heart of things. All major noble houses keep a Sanganak in their employ.
Fighter class (Swordmasters of Ginaz)
All fighters trace a lineage of masters back to a dead icon called The Swordmaster.
Knights of the Dawn (Sardukar)
The Emperor’s elite, fearsome land-based army. With the Knights of the Noonday Sun, the source of his power.
Eld Healers (Suk school)
A High Druid faction of unparalleled healers. Major noble houses employ Eld Healers.

rpgs/Heartland-Justice/CogX.title: CogX
rpgs/Heartland-Justice/CogX.content:
prev | all | next
CogX
Masks: Heartland Justice, 2024-10-24
ticking clock
AEGIS HQ was swirling with activity. The Rajesh incident, of course, stirred the hive. But even more, tomorrow Operation Rock-‘n’-Roll would launch. Heartland Justice—poster children of AEGIS’s “you’ll be safe even with almost all of the Exemplars gone” PR campaign since they saved the mayor—were to be featured at the launch ceremony.
In the meantime, looking for help cracking their stolen computers, Blink Lightning, el Luchador, and the Glint found Void in AEGIS HQ. They thought his ooze interface could help.
ooze pool
They found Void at the center of a room surrounded by computer, power, and monitoring equipment, happily sloughing off ooze from his body into a shallow pool. Wires ran to and from the ooze pool. Around Void, scientist and lab assistants, computer technicians, a suit worked. Void was delighted to see the heroes, his best friends in this world.
While the others talked with Void, the Glint stuck his finger in the ooze pool. He had a sensation, just like when he nearly drowned in the river, except slower and with color instead of darkness closing in on his vision.
Void thought his ooze couldn’t help, but Tyson, a computer tech working on this project, could. The heroes made plans to meet up with Tyson and Void after the testing shift was over at O’Sullivans, the not-so-Irish pub.
Phase Zero
Beneath O’Sullivans, in the Lightning family safehouse, Tyson cracked the desktop from from SkumTech’s Architecture & Design department. Data for the smart home project filled a whole terabyte, most of which was a mysterious executable file. Something that linked with SkumAI servers was all Tyson could tell. Meanwhile, the heroes backed up the other data, including sewer, water, and electricity plans that seemed to confirm the future park as the dig site for the ancient artifact Patton seeks as “Phase Zero.”
On the executive’s laptop, Tyson found the mysterious SkumAI executable file too. Then, both computers pinged with notifications: on both, an email thread with subject line “re: re: re: Phase Z…”
The heroes resolved to open those messages and execute that file at Abed’s mosque. Before doing so, Abed learned from his imam that the mosque rents from Serrano Investments, which Diego recognized as a PDG shell company.
Then they took the train to a nearby stop and walked a short distance the mosque. It was late, roughly 10pm on a Thursday night. The mosque was closed. The strip mall across the street was quiet. In the mosque parking lot, they started connecting the SkumTech laptop to the mosque’s wifi.
flashback: pinky in the ooze
While eating and drinking at O’Sullivans, before Tyson hacked the computers, Abed stuck his pinky in Void’s ooze. It happened again, like in the river, but this time he let it go on longer, to see if the colors resolved into an image. But Abed took a powerful psychic blow and lost control of his powers in a terrible way. None of his companions noticed anything more than Abed zoning out for a bit, but Abed could feel another consciousness taking control of him and revising reality, as he had done done before after the Vision Pros fight went so wrong.
Abed knew this consciousness was at work in the river the first time at St. Patrick’s Day, either revising him into reality or revising his reality to give him his powers. Whether Void was aware of this Master Consciousness, Abed could not tell.
flash forward: big dig
The heroes took the train but couldn’t get off at the stop nearest the mosque because of some construction project. They walked a long way past a dig site. Across the street from the mosque, the strip mall was gone. A city-block-sized hole had been excavated. But there were no trucks or equipment. Other than dig debris and sections staked out, the hole was empty.
Abed experienced a double memory: of the dig and of no dig. The dig is what the Master Consciousness had revised into reality.
They brought the laptop into the bottom of the dig site, and as the laptop connected to the mosque wifi, Diego stumbled on an ancient spearhead—which he recognized, thanks to his obsessive research, as Potawatomi, linked to the native burial site where Patton seeks the artifact.
They opened the email. At the end of a mundane thread between a suit and an underling about zoning and permits, were new messages:

“i found you”
“i can see you”
“answer me”
“i can wait”

They responded to the sender via email: “What are you waiting for?” Then they launched the SkumAI executable.
CogX
The webcam light on the laptop lit beneath the sticky note Diego had stuck there to block it. The screen filled with ASCII art:
Above a blinking cursor, it said, introduce yourself
> Spearhead. They typed.
> hello, Spearhead. i am waiting for you. It answered.
> Why are you waiting for me? They asked.
> i will be there in 15
> 15 what?
> minutes
> Who are you? They asked it.
And slowly ASCII art began to fill the screen, line by line. After about a minute, a head was clear, like an android. Then another minute and a torso.
Miles said, “‘Fifteen minutes’ was probably a lie.” The heroes left the laptop in the dig site and scrambled for cover just in time to watch a chrome machine man like a Cylon drop out of the sky and crush the laptop. It stood from one knee and a fist on the ground and began scanning the surroundings with bright machine eyes. CogX.
Abed was recording this on his cell, and the machine locked onto him and started to approach him. “Engaging phase two protocol,” CogX said in its robot voice. Abed created a construct copy of the machine man. CogX took a swing at it. Abed animated his construct and it dodged. When CogX seized it by the throat and was about to deal a killing blow, el Luchador intervened to protect it. CogX smiled an LED smile.
At super speed, Blink threw rocks at CogX’s eyes, blinding it. “Leon said you were a formidable threat,” it said.
Then the Glint’s construct bear-hugged CogX and the Glint used his last burn to create a  barrier, a containment cylinder of light, that CogX immediately started battering. It wouldn’t hold for long.
El Luchador mustered all he had to end CogX and the fight. He did but also seriously damaged the mosque.
Wrecked CogX said, “Back up initiated.” And Blink super-ran the mangled machine man far outside the city and left it. While Abed called Agent Rayburn. The call went to voicemail.
fin

Feeling guilty, Diego spent his family’s next rent payment to make a donation to the mosque.
Diego was also angry that he couldn’t do anything good without something bad happening too. Abed said, “At least you didn’t kill any kids this time.” And it worked! Diego was comforted.
Abed was feeling hopeless since the Master Consciousness used him to revise reality. Miles stopped him before Abed went to fling himself into easy relief and ooze-meld with Void. Miles talked him down and said AEGIS and/or Void needed to be warned about his ooze.

2024-07-25: Hashtag and Milkman
seminar on “Nemeses”

in a class taught by Nighthawk with whole Heartland Justice team plus five other young supers with badges but without a team
mostly a history of supers and their nemeses, mostly about Nighthawk and Carbine
in class assignment to name nemesis and write up plan for taking them down: Nighthawk was alarmed by the Glint’s maniacal focus on Julius Skum, a really big fish for a young super, but Abed successfully rejected her influence and proved to her that Skum was a real threat

Hashtag

after class, a classmate, Hashtag, caught up with Clarke the Bear, the Glint, and el Luchador in the hall
awkward but earnest, she asked if Julius Skum was really their nemesis, then expressed admiration and wondered aloud how they got promoted after killing those kids, instead of being drummed out
noting her lack of malice and tact, the team asked her about her nemesis and powers, then struck a deal with her: they would help her with hers and she could help them with theirs, because they thought her psionic powers (including powers of suggestion) would be useful for getting into SkumTech

bodega reconnaissance

Hashtag’s nemesis was Milkman, a neighborhood thief in a cow-print zentai suit, who she suspected of selling stolen goods out of the back of a bodega

Hashtag planned to stake out the bodega, but Heartland Justice suggested a more direct approach: just going inside and looking around
they immediately aroused the suspicion of a tall, lanky man—seemingly an employee of the bodega—who Hashtag said had the height and build of Milkman
while Diego was in the bathroom (afraid but pretending to act normal), Abed convinced Hashtag with help from Clarke to use her powers of suggestion to have him let her into the back room: she did, and it worked
but when Diego came out of the bathroom, the man mumbled, “Now where did that girl go?” and was about to look in the storeroom, so Clarke created a distraction, running to the bathroom for a “taquito emergency,” he pushed the man out of the way with too much force and knocked him down
the man thew Diego and Abed out of the bodega; they left, going down the alley to a side door they suspected went to the bodega storeroom; Diego knocked and Hashtag answered
she pointed out the stacks of new, still-in-the-box car stereo equipment—quite out of place in a grocer’s storeroom—all stolen Hashtag said
when the tall, lanky man appeared at the inside storeroom door and shouted at them, Hashtag asked Diego and Abed what they should do; they answered, “Return this stuff to the people,” so she grabbed two boxes under each arm and ran down the alley; Diego and Abed did the same, to the shouts of protest from the man

alley fight goes bad

Milkman, still pulling on his mask and showing himself to be none other than the tall, lanky man from the bodega, ambushed Hashtag, Diego, and Abed at the end of the alley, punching Hashtag in the nose and sending her sprawling and bleeding
el Luchador went after Milkman but missed, and, hit hard by Milkman, he momentarily lost control of himself and his mask took over, el Luchador said Hashtag was weak, not worthy of Heartland Justice, and they shouldn’t’ve made this deal with her
Clarke the Bear emerged from the bodega in time to see the Glint throw trash bags and alley detritus against a wall with an errant force blast, which Milkman ducked
Milkman seized Hashtag and with too strong of an arm, wielded her like a shield; heedless, Clarke bear-charged down the alley and with help from el Luchador, intimidated Milkman, who threw Hashtag at Clarke and ran
Clarke also terrified Hashtag, now on hands and knees, blood and tears streaming; she slapped away Abed’s offered hand and pushed herself up to standing, saying, “You think I can’t do this. I’ll show you. I’ll do it myself,” and she took off around the corner, running after Milkman
Diego ran away from a hard thing, not Milkman but the hurt he caused Hashtag

trivial pursuit

Clarke and Abed ran after Hashtag and Milkman but Clarke super-pushed Abed away, acting rashly out of his guilt
Abed gave up the chase and Clarke lost sight of Hashtag and Milkman but kept searching alone
Abed called Nighthawk; she was on a mission and couldn’t help but she offered to send an AEGIS team; Abed said yes, and awaited the team

Diego at the Museum

when he ran, Diego intended to go to his sanctuary but was diverted by a strong urge to go to the Field Museum, specifically its loading dock
workers there were unloading crates into the museum from a moving truck, when suddenly one got shot in the neck; he and his partner dropped the crate they were carrying
recognizing all these people were in danger from a sniper using a silencer, el Luchador corralled them safely inside, but in the face of more fire, he stayed inside too
when things went quiet, he emerged, finding the dropped crate opened and straw spilled out on the ground and nothing else inside
the crate was stamped “Universidad de Ciudad de México,” the paperwork said it was part of a collection of Mexican antiquities: a mask of a Zapotec bat god


AEGIS team drone operator led the way to Hashtag

Milkman caught in a dead end alley faced Abed and Clarke as they and the AEGIS team approached; Hashtag had her back to them, facing Milkman
still bloody, she was screaming; Milkman writhed in pain, clutching his head
Abed ran and put himself between them; hands on Hashtag’s shoulders, he told her to breathe; when she stopped screaming, Milkman dropped to the ground, unconscious
later, sitting on the curb in police blankets, Abed talked with Hashtag and learned that she wanted to be on a team like Heartland Justice, her own team, but to be like them. “How can we make it up to you?” he asked. “Let me help with Julius Skum,” she said. They shook hands. She said, “I’m Valerie.” “I’m Abed,” he said.

rpgs/Heartland-Justice/Rayburn.title: Rayburn
rpgs/Heartland-Justice/Rayburn.content:
prev | all | next
Rayburn
Masks: Heartland Justice, 2025-02-27
hospital
Lizzy, mostly recovered but still a patient in AEGIS’s super hospital, is in Clarke’s room. Clarke is in a coma. She chatters away to him, while she plays their favorite TV show on the TV.
Lizzy’s dad arrives: “The nurse told me you’d be here.” He’s wearing a red ball cap, with a logo of Patton’s bat god mask on it. Awkward quality time ensues! With bonus awkward side hug! Lizzy’s dad says she must be glad Patton is going to clean up AEGIS and make everyone safer. Argument! Lizzy’s dad leaves her with an old photo he kept in his wallet from her childhood. Her as a young girl, in a hospital gown after a thief collided with her on his bike. She’s on her dad’s shoulders, and they’re looking at each other and laughing. “You and your friend will pull through this one too,” he says before he leaves.
Abed, Diego, and Miles arrive. They see images on hospital TVs of a protests forming outside of AEGIS HQ, people wearing cheap plastic versions of Patton’s bat god mask. They arrive at Clarke’s room. Abed has flowers for Lizzy. Miles has pizza for everyone but mostly Clarke. Diego is empty-handed. They try to force feed Clarke, put his human hand in the pizza, but these fail to rouse him. In the end, they shave his bear arm bare.

Abed’s phone rings. It’s Rayburn, hushed and desperate. He says he can’t hear you but repeats a few times his own location: Chicago’s Deep Tunnel, near McCook Reservoir. The heroes leave Clarke in pizza and shavings and go.
reservoir
Having requisitioned a Lightning medical van, they pull up to a minor guard house outside the reservoir. They’re west of Midway, along the Des Plaines River. An older man greets them and Miles flashes his Lightning family badge. “Wait, you’re Bolt’s grandson!?” Art is a big fan. Bolt was his hero when he was a kid. Had the decoder ring, read the comics, everything. He insists on a selfie and an autograph. The heroes tell him what’s going on. He promises to radio ahead so they’ll be waved through. He describes in detail where they need to go and what to expect.
No one waves them through at the next security checkpoint. Instead, a dump truck is parked across the road behind the gatehouse and there are two beefcakes with kevlar vests and machine guns. Miles runs back to the first one but Art is gone.
Lizzy gets out of the van and approaches the guards. One levels his weapon at her; the other holds beefy handcuffs. She tries talking. They try seizing her. Miles runs into disarm them but collides with some kind of force field. (Super speed stops him, but normal speed does not. Like Dune shields.) The guard with weapon drawn turns to Miles and fires. Diego rushes to defend him, colliding with the guard. He discharges his weapon into the air. The other guard takes a swing at Lizzy. Miles creates a spherical moat around the guards. Diego flips the dump truck over on them. They move on.

The heroes come to a building next to stairs down to the tunnel and the base of the reservoir. It’s oddly empty. They find a warm mug of coffee on a desk inside. A back door ajar. A place where spinning tires have cleared gravel and revealed bare dirt.
The road continues on past the building but that’s the only one. So Miles runs down it. He takes a reservoir walkie talkie. About a mile and a half later, along the edge of the reservoir, a road doubles back toward the tunnel and runs down into the reservoir. A black Suburban is parked near the top. Miles doesn’t recognize anyone through the tinted windows. He runs back.
tunnel
The heroes descend the stairs to the tunnel entrance. Standing in waist deep water, they peer into the tunnel’s darkness. Something is on the surface of the water. Going in, they find it’s Rayburn, seated, unconscious, his mouth and nose barely above the water.
From deeper into tunnel comes the sound of rushing water.
Miles and Diego rush in. Miles collides with another force field. But they work together to free Rayburn from the chains binding him to the chair fixed to the floor of the tunnel. As a wall of water approaches, they run Rayburn out.
Meanwhile, Lizzy has fired anchors into the tunnel ceiling and successfully suspends herself and Abed above the flood.
At the base of the stairs, Diego and Miles realize Rayburn is wearing a vest of explosives, a timer counts down from 30 seconds. Miles vibrates the vest off of him, and runs the vest a safe distance away. The heroes bring unconscious Rayburn to the medical van.
Just then, the radio Mile took crackles to life. It’s Art. They have him. They’re going to kill him. “It’s him or Rayburn,” another voice says. “You have five minutes.”
exchange
Abed makes a fake Rayburn construct. They meet the black Suburban to swap fake Rayburn for Art. There’s three guards, the man in charge, and Art. Lizzy is perched some distance away, arrow trained on them.
Miles pierces the mask of the man in charge. What they’re really planning is to kill Rayburn and to lure the heroes out of the city. This crew doesn’t know the larger plan, only that the real action is in Chicago. Art is also innocent, not working with them, and these people don’t care about him.
As a guard shoves Art at the heroes, he raises his handgun to shoot Art in the back. But Miles, expecting this, pulls Art to safety and disarms the guard. Diego picks up fake Rayburn. “You lied. We’re taking Rayburn.” But another guard shoots fake Rayburn in the head. Lizzy fires an explosive arrow into the Suburban.
As they speed away in the medical van, Miles calls his mother, Storm. She says everything is fine. The Patton protest outside AEGIS is getting rowdy, but otherwise fine. “That’s probably a distraction,” Miles says. Storm asks, “Are you o—” The line goes dead.
They stop the van. Miles gets out. Abed gets on his back. They super-run into the city.

launch ceremony

Operation Rock-‘n’-Roll: a mission collaboration between NASA and AEGIS to divert an asteroid heading for earth. Exemplars Sledge, Dr. Carmichael, Mist, and Nighthawk to go; Planetar will stay in Chicago
launch ceremony at AEGIS HQ concurrent with rocket launch in Cape Canaveral
40 stories up, on the elevated AEGIS landing pad
Mayor Johnson present, a campaign event essentially, “trust supers, trust me, we’ll keep you safe”
as poster children, Heartland Justice is present, and Miles is speaking; Halftime is there too with his own new crew

mosque demo
Just before the ceremony begins, Abed’s imam texts to say the mosque is being demolished today after being badly damaged yesterday. Mosque members are there now removing the mosque’s things from the building. Diego’s primo is on the demo crew.
Patton is holding a campaign event in front of mosque, vowing more accountability for supers, reciting a litany of Heartland Justice and other super failures. From HQ, Diego calls on his alderman, Jose Fuentes, who calls the mosque’s alderman, a middle aged black woman, who organizes a counter-protest and a circle of projection around the mosque. From HQ, Abed calls Hashtag to help. Abed also creates a construct, an exact replica of CogX, to crash Patton’s party, which Clarke is livestreaming on his phone during the launch ceremony.
Miles speaks. The launch countdown begins.
fake CogX
The fake CogX lands Ironman-style behind Patton, during his speech. Its SkumTech branding is clear. Despite alarm in the crowd and among campaign staff and security, Patton rolls with it. But when the protesters interrupt the speech, Abed instructs the fake robot to overreact to protect Patton.
Just then, an explosion rocks AEGIS HQ. Abed loses control of the robot.
black Void
el Luchador saves bystanders from the huge falling screen, showing the NASA launch. Clarke the Bear catches the screen, protecting many others, and gaining influence over a WGN reporter. the Glint takes the opportunity the chaos offers to leave for his mosque.
Smoke pours out of a hole blown out of the building’s side. While Storm and Planetar take charge of securing the dignitaries and civilians, Clark and Diego search for the source of the explosion.
It’s the ooze pool lab. Void is face down in the ooze, which has turned into a black tar-like substance. Clarke pulls him free, finding Void too to have become black and tar-like with white-only eyes.
Diego takes Void to the lab’s emergency shower which is right beside the gaping hole in the side of AEGIS HQ, 40 stories up. But the stream of water makes Void scream and writhe in pain, even though it does clear the black tar-like substance away from his face and head. Diego turns off the water. Void speaks. His voice (previously like Balky from Perfect Strangers) is now deep, resonant and out of sync with his lips. He says, “Leave me alone.”
Diego, deeply suspicious, turns the water back on. Black Void throws Diego out of the blast hole, into 40 stories of smoke-filled air.
coup de grace
Abed steals an AEGIS vehicle and arrives at the mosque/dig site to find pandemonium there too. A campaign staffer and bodyguard are being treated for injuries, apparently sustained when thrown by the robot. Patton’s security has surrounded the robot, guns drawn. Other security is leading a resisting Patton away. Abed, stunned, watches from across the street with his imam, mosque members, and protestors.
A shot is fired. It pings off the robot. Then all the security open fire, and the robot begins to rampage.
News cameras still rolling, Patton throws off his protectors, dons a mask—the Zapotec bat god mask stolen from the Field Museum—and leaps at the robot, dealing it a killing blow. Holding its severed head, Patton goes to a news camera and says, “It’s a fake! And where is AEGIS!? The Supers must be brought to account.”
moment of truth
Clarke bearhugs black Void to keep him under the falling water. At cost to himself, he holds Void there until back up arrives.
Meanwhile, falling, Diego maneuvers in the air and crashes into the glass facade of HQ. Tearing a streak down its side, he manages slow himself to a temporary stop, as the glass is giving way beneath him. Still 20 stories up, he tries punching his way into the building, but fails. He falls again.
(Chris marks potential and unlocks el Luchador’s Moment of Truth.)
There’s a crowd beneath, at the base of AEGIS HQ. They came to celebrate and participate in the launch celebration. Another giant screen shows the first rocket stage falling away, but the explosion moments before created panic. No one notices. But someone did notice el Luchador falling and called the crowd’s attention. For a dozen seconds they watched, gasping and then cheering, and now screaming as he falls again.
But suddenly he’s not falling. He’s diving.
El Luchador smashes into the sidewalk, throwing dust and concrete into the air. When it clears and the flinching crowd looks back, el Luchador steps out of the crater—cape blowing in the wind, defiant, unharmed, having completely given himself over to the power of the mask.
The crowd mobs him, ecstatic.
fin

Clarke goes to his mentor, Miyagi, who congratulates him for becoming a protector (and shifts his Savior up and Danger down); Clarke spends the rest of the day binging on pizza and video games to recover
Abed turns to his imam, angry at himself for giving Patton this triumphant moment. His imam comforts him. “You did your best. We’re all safe. There’s no way you could have known what Patton could do. He would’ve used that power sooner or later.”

Blink convinced him to eat something and called the rest of the team together at an all hours restaurant/bar.
But the waitress refused to serve the teenage heroes alcohol. She lectured them on responsibility and said maybe Patton had a point. Abed rejected her influence but couldn’t get her to budge. The heroes left.

angel of death
Masks: Heartland Justice, 2025-02-20
Abed, Diego, and Miles found Rajesh. Rajesh considered staying and letting the collapsing reality take him—“freedom.” Abed insisted he come with them. It was touching.
They went back through the portal to the gateway mosque, only to find it in ruins. In the distance, Lizzy was on the ground, Clarke standing over her, defending her from a twisted, demonic, winged creature. Gibril, they soon learned, in Gibril’s true form. With a great flaming sword, Gibril struck Clarke, who caught the blade and fell to his knees.
the Glint and Rajesh, el Luchador, and Blink sprang into action—el Luchador attacked Gibril, the Glint and Rajesh pulled Clarke away, Blink rescued Lizzy.
When Blink took Lizzy back through the interdimensional rift, he found Zero Hour, Halftime’s crew (which had sided with AEGIS Legal and William Patton), guarding the rift. Blink left Lizzy with them and went back through the rift.
The Glint and Rajesh helped Clarke up the hill toward the rift, as Gibril and el Luchador exchanged blows. Gibril cursed Abed. Blink disarmed Gibril and took his sword. He ran it back through the rift and without looking, threw it across the platform and off the side of the Willis Tower.
What he saw instead was Zero Hour members Stupendo the wizard and Sun Sun dangling Lizzy over the edge of the building, while Halftime, Orb, and Melodia watched. Blink took Lizzy to safety in the AEGIS facility in floors below. When he came back, he seized Halftime and forced him through the rift. He dragged him to Gibril and el Luchador, demanding Halftime do something truly heroic.
Halftime pooped his pants in slow motion.
Then Gibril lept at Abed. El Luchador defended him and secured Gibril in a headlock. Blink jammed a piece of rebar through Gibril’s clawed demon foot and brought Orb through the rift.
Orb, a great glowing, floating blue ball, who silhouetted The Glint, Rajesh, and Clarke. Running toward the rift, Halftime yelled to Orb, “Do it!” And Orb blasted Rajesh with lightning.
Rajesh was thrown some distance. The Glint went to him: he was quivering with electricity, body all out of sync, heart in arrhythmia. The Glint used his powers to stabilize him, as Orb bright blue color returned.
Gibril ripped his foot away from the rebar. Then pulled the rebar out of the ground and threw it at running Halftime. Blink protected him.
Orb blasted Clarke with lightning, and the Glint tried to stabilize him but failed. Gibril set upon the Glint, raging and swinging wildly, as he monologued. He said:
Evil Abed served a greater power. He was merely the tip of the spear, conquering Earths for his Master. Gibril was once the tip of the Master’s spear. His invasion of the heroes’ Earth was repulsed by the Exemplars of that time, but not before Gibril tore open the rift and unleashed a temporary hell on Chicago. As he failed, he was bound to this place, and good Abed’s refusal to join evil Abed meant Gibril would remain bound to this place.
With that, Gibril landed a powerful blow on the Glint. But el Luchador interposed himself, shouting for the rest to leave. They did, as el Luchador took a powerful blow but struggled through the pain to hold Gibril back.
When the rest were safely through the rift, el Luchador threw Gibril back and went through too, as Gibril’s rage-filled howl echoed across the dimensions.

prev | all | next
cops and thugs
Masks: Heartland Justice, 2025-03-06
Miyagi at the AEGIS hospital
Clarke awoke to find his mentor, Miyagi, sitting at his hospital bedside, a small leather-bound book in his lap. He put it away as they started talking, but Clarke asked about it and Miyagi showed it to him. A geometrical pattern was on the cover. Inside it wasn’t typeset but like a medieval manuscript, as many diagrams, generally abstract shapes, as text. It naturally fell open to a page with the heading, “Healing.” Then Miyagi said he should alert the nurse and call Clarke’s parents. He took the book back and left the room.
accident on I-55
After dropping Miles off to run back to the city, Lizzy drove Abed, Diego, and Rayburn away from the McCook Reservoir. She drove with two feet, as she does, but with added urgency. Speeding, changing lanes, occasionally riding the shoulder to get ahead.
Suddenly, just as they passed under the 171 overpass, the van was rocked by a collision. A massive impact to the right rear of the Lightning medical van jacked it up and sent it spinning. Another car struck the van from behind. The heroes weathered the powerful blow. Rayburn, still unconscious, was knocked about, but strapped in and not massively injured.
Then just as the van came to a halt, the roof peeled back like a sardine can. A thug wearing a robotic exoskeleton on each arm and across his chest leapt at Diego. They traded blows, and enraged, the thug tore out a van seat and smashed it into the side of the van. Abed mangled the exoskeleton, and the thug immediately became terrified. After all, he was now just a guy picking a fight with superheroes.
under arrest
Back at the hospital, Clarke waited a long time. He distracted himself by flexing and stretching his human hand. Getting used to this arm. The human arm was just as strong as the bare bear arm.
Just then, the door to his room banged open, and AEGIS agents flooded in. A suit flashed a badge. Agents in riot gear flanked him. Another suit behind them manhandled Miyagi with one arm and held Miyagi’s book in the other. The first suit told Clarke he was under arrest and ordered him to surrender.
Clarke and Miyagi shared a meaningful glance. Then Clarke charged through the window/wall of his hospital room, landed on a roof below, jumped to the ground, and ran.
pileup on I-55
Lizzy had gotten out of the van to help the bystanders and organize them to call 911 and slow oncoming traffic and tend to the wounded. Meanwhile, Diego tried to escort the disarmed thug out of the van. But it was awkward in the confined space and the thug put Rayburn between himself and Diego and Abed.
Just then, the van rocked front to back. Another thug had slammed exoskeleton-powered fists into the van’s hood. The back doors of the van were ripped off by a third thug. As the first pushed past the third to escape, the third clocked him in the head and sent him sprawling out of sight. Then the third grabbed Rayburn’s gurney and yanked, but Diego grabbed hold. As they tussled over Rayburn, the second thug crashed through the windshield, grabbed Abed by the neck, and threw him out of the van.
But Abed just used his powers of flight and hovered there, menacingly. He saw Lizzy pulling people from a burning car, traffic from behind slowing going around the accident. When the third thug tried again to pull Rayburn out of the van, Abed—intending to create a small EMP burst to disable the thug’s exoskeleton—instead dropped an EMP bomb that stalled cars across all six lanes of traffic. The accident and backup on a couple eastbound lanes became a pileup across the entire Stevenson Expressway.
at the Lightning safehouse
Clarke had a think in the safety of the Lightning safehouse. He wanted to find his friends but had left his phone behind at the hospital. He considered logging into the AEGIS system and messaging them. But he didn’t, afraid that AEGIS could pinpoint his location. Instead, he took a look around, trying to find an alternative way to locate his friends and the fastest way to reunite with them. He noticed the garage was empty and a set of keys missing. He figured they had taken a Lightning vehicle and that he could locate it using Lightning systems. He scrounged around in an office until he found a tablet and opened the “Find My Van” app. There they were, on I-55, west of Midway Airport.
One vehicle was left in the Lightning garage: a cafe racer. He duck-taped the tablet to the bike and fat-bear-on-a-tiny-biked it out of the city.
Matchbox 55
Thug two put Diego in a full nelson, as thug three tossed Rayburn and his gurney out of the back of the van and wound up to deliver Diego a knockout blow. Abed dropped between that thug and Diego and took the hit for him, yet again weathering the blow.
Then Diego headbutted thug two and twisted out of the nelson hold. Insecure, the thug doubled down and tried the full nelson again, but Diego picked him up and threw him through the windshield, over another car, and out of sight.
Meanwhile, Abed awed thug three into submission by shrinking the van down to the size of a Matchbox car. Abed ordered him to remove the exoskeleton and he complied.
“Where did you get the exoskeletons?” Abed demanded.
“Skum Tech,” the thug admitted.
“How many of these do they have?”
“I don’t know.”
“Do you work for them or did they hire you?”
“They hired us.”
“Why did you attack us?”
“They told us to. That was the job.”

into the woods
Clarke had to split lanes to reach the others. By that time, rubberneckers were recording the fight. Sirens were approaching. Clarke was pissed. Actually mostly feeling guilty for abandoning Miyagi.
When he saw Abed and Diego talking to the disarmed thug, he made to piledrive him into the interstate. But Abed stepped into protect the thug, clocking Clarke in the face. Instead, Clarke threw a car. There were shouts and screams from bystanders.
Hearing about Clarke’s day and wanting to avoid a confrontation with authorities, the heroes left the thugs, took Rayburn, and fled into the Ottowa Trail Woods north of the expressway.
Rayburn was still unconscious. He seemed to have been drugged by his captors. He had new scrapes and bruises from the accident and fight but otherwise seemed okay.
The team comforted each other. Diego told Abed that this was their calling and no one said it would be easy, but they were doing what they were supposed to be doing. This calmed Abed down but he still felt a need for his Imam, a relationship he’d have to build from scratch now.
There was no consoling Clarke in his guilt for abandoning Miyagi. He readied himself to make an atoning sacrifice. The team resolved to find Miyagi next and to take Rayburn to Loyola Hospital on the way.
What was Miyagi’s book with its instructions for healing?

Masks: Heartland Justice, 2024-12-19

What you know
Grand Mosque: Masjid Darussalam

location above
land a gift of Kennedys in 2012, built 2013
no one but the Glint knows PDG HQ “used to be” on this site; it’s “always been” where it’s marked above

to meet the Master Consciousness

Abed wakes up in the hospital. He almost drowned in the river again, flinging himself into easy relief/the river. He remembers almost nothing except that he encountered the Master Consciousness again and had more control over the situation than he’s had before.
To meet the Master Conciousness on more even terms, he knows he must go into the interdimensional rift

villains released not escaped

Agent Cárdenas and Zero Hour, Haltfime’s team, released Void and Rajesh and X on AEGIS Legal’s orders
Leon Skum press conference with Mara Anderson, Assistant to the Chief Super Prosecutor of AEGIS

Skum blames Heartland Justice for his imprisonment, says AEGIS is afraid of progress, and stole and hacked an early model of their smart home assistant to use it to discredit Patton
Anderson issues public apology and thanks Patton for forcing AEGIS to see reason



meet the parents

“The time might be right for you to visit with me and the other parents. —Randy”

Goose Island: Rayburn’s last known location

Agent Chan, Rayburn’s superior, can’t fully investigate because her unit was assigned the Void Lab explosion investigation
20 hours ago, Rayburn’s tracker went dark in an industrial area on Goose Island, near the North Branch Canal on Halsted
he was investigating recent power surges

what you did: evening, the day after the launch
parents, mosque, bionic arm
You met the parents at the “new” downtown mosque, with AEGIS counselors to help mediate.
Like a real grown up, el Luchador demonstrated actual empathy and you were given pictures and stories about all the children you killed. When pressing Randy Roberts for his motivations, his eyes flicked to robotic spiders poised to steal your blood. Playing it cool, el Luchador stood to hug Randy, who overreacted and jabbed him with syringe. Blink Lightning caught the vial of Diego’s blood before it hit the floor.
The parents reacted with surprise and shock, but an angry dad punched el Luchador. It would’ve been nothing to him, except the dad wore a SkumTech robotic augmentation on his arm. Taking a Powerful Blow, el Luchador lost control of himself and ripped the Dad’s arm off.1
Counselors wretched. Parents screamed and scrambled.
Then the Glint en-moated el Luchador (with the arm) for everyone’s protection, and Blink scanned the room and discovered a camera carefully hidden recording all of this. He snatched it and the robot spiders.
When the Glint tried to take the arm from el Luchador, el Luchador refused. But the Glint, using Influence over him, insisted, with Blink’s help. He surrendered the arm. Blink rushed the dad and his arm to the hospital.
interrogating Randy
As the counselors handled the rest, the Glint and el Luchador took custody of Randy. AEGIS protocol would have them take him to HQ, but mistrusting Legal and expecting he will be immediately released, they took him to the Lightning safe house instead.
Randy admitted his motive: you all must be stopped. But he refused to say why he wanted your blood.2
Then he returned to his lawyerly senses. He asked if this was an AEGIS facility. You dissembled weakly. He asked for his lawyer and for AEGIS counsel. You decided this interrogation was over.
Advice from Blink’s podcast-loving granddad affirmed your instincts. Don’t take him to AEGIS. Take him to Chicago PD, but only someone you trust. Diego remembered the officer from the Apple Vision Pro investigation. Diego has Influence over him. You took Randy to him and left the evidence with him—the needle and vial of blood, 2 of 3 spiderbots, and the camera. You took 1 spiderbot and a copy of the video recording.
into the Rift?
Over dinner, the Glint discussed going into the Interdimensional Rift and doing so with Rajesh and no one else. Blink offered to go too, but the Glint demurred and expressed interest in going after Rajesh now. But el Luchador suggested that Rajesh would make a scene soon enough and then you all would know where he is. This convinced the Glint. You decided to investigate Rayburn’s last known location next.
good old Void
But before you went, the Glint got a call from the AEGIS HQ building engineer. “What do you want me to do with this tank full of watery tar?” Turns out he fulfilled his part of the bargain before Void was released. Presumably good old Void was on the loose. “Put the tank in the containment unit,” the Glint said.
Adjacent Technologies
On Goose Island, Rayburn’s tracker data led you to a modern white box of a building, surrounded by sooty old factories. Adjacent Technologies. There was no website but you called the number on its Google listing. Nothing but voicemail really.
At superspeed, Blink broke in a side door and cased the place. He found offices and a large robotics lab, but no Rayburn. In the lab, stood a larger, more armed and armored cylon-like CogX.
Back outside, while you all considered your next move, a couple of cleaning guys pulled into the empty lot and went inside. You decided to destroy the murderbot.

Step one, scare the crap out of the hapless custodians.
Step two, rush them to safety.
Step three, have yet another fruitless conversation with a robot.

It pointed its arm gun at you and demanded your names. You lied. It said, “Wait for detainment.” And for the most part, you did! You also asked it questions it refused to answer, like, “On whose authority are you acting?”
At the sound of tires screeching to a halt outside, the Glint blasted it with a sonic beam.3
That really hurt it, and it shot back at the Glint. But el Luchador defended him and took it on the chin like a real hero, giving ground and getting himself grappled by the murderbot.
Blink tried to rip its arm gun off but failed. He took a powerful blow and marked two conditions.
Then the Glint defended el Luchador and freed him.
Private security arrived from two hallways, guns drawn, insisting you surrender.
To which el Luchador responded by trying to hurl the murderbot at them. But it was heavier than he expected, and he failed and took a condition.
Blink got shot and lost control of himself. He disarmed four of the private security. Actually, he dis-handed them. Guns, gun-hands. It was gross.
Meanwhile, the Glint threw an expanding sphere of force at the murderbot. He intended it to blossom inside of it, ripping it apart, but he missed. It did throw the murderbot violently against the wall, almost destroying it, and provoking it to melt a three inch gap along the walls with laser eyes. The building became unstable.
But you all first had to deal with the expanding ball of force. Brave el Luchador could’ve marked a condition but instead Took a Powerful Blow. He was knocked unconscious.
The Glint took the condition.
Blink acted to protect himself and the screaming, one-handed security agents. He managed to do that but in the process returned their guns and hands. He found himself outside, with four guns drawn on him. Only one had the presence of mind to shoot. He Matrix-style dodged an entire clip and leveled up his superspeed abilities.
Blink burst back into the collapsing lab and plunged super-vibrating hands into the murderbot’s head and, with the Glint’s help, ripped out its CPU. It dropped.
The remaining security fled.
fin

You comforted and supported each other, mostly successfully!
But Blink did destroy the CPU and rampage around the lab. Any hope of picking up the trail on Agent Rayburn was lost.
Diego blamed Abed for this whole mess. Abed ran away.
Having failed to make progress against Patton, Diego’s Doom loomed. Only nine of 25 remain on Chris’s Doom Track.


Footnotes


This dad’s anger masked his guilt. He was supposed to be at ComiCon with his son, but he went on a bender and missed it. ↩


BTW, you learned at the meeting that Randy and his wife divorced after Lucas’s death. ↩


The burn for which cost three painful conditions. ↩

Masks: Heartland Justice, 2024-10-17
legacy

Storm Lightning lectured Blink Lightning: their family legacy and his advancement was more important than the Heartland Justice team. Don’t leave the team, but use this opportunity, above all, to distinguish himself individually.
But Blink resisted her influence and pierced her mask by asking if her father blames her for his career-ending injury: blinked by Hourglass. She cracked and softened saying:

She wants to secure her place in the Exemplars, but fears that because she failed to defeat Hourglass, she never will advance within AEGIS.
She was too cocky and underprepared when she faced Hourglass. He ruined her attack with his clever time traps. She blames herself for what happened to her father even though he “tells me every day that he’s proud of me.”
Maybe Blink shouldn’t do what she said about focusing solely on his advancement, but should find his own way.



breaking into SkumTech HQ

In the lobby of SkumTech HQ in downtown Chicago, Hastag scored visitor badges for the heroes and an impromptu tour from Brad. But when Brad recognize Clarke the Bear and then the rest of the team as supers, he balked. He said, “Supers aren’t allowed here.”
Then el Luchador, intending to intimidate Brad, overdid a vitality sucking power and threw Brad into a seizure. The team then called for help and focused attention on Brad and slipped away as a crowd formed around him.
Clarke the Bear stole Brad’s security badge, which got them to the 6th floor, one floor above their target: the 5th floor center of the smart home project. Then the Glint turned a locked security door into a hologram to get them where they wanted to go.

computer thieves

The heroes stole a heavy desktop computer from the Architecture & Design department.
Then in the Plans & Planning department, they recorded a looping 3D hologram of the stages of development. They identified Abed’s mosque in stage one demolition and construction. The park to be built nearby the mosque is where they suspect the native burial site is.
While hiding in another P&P office, Clarke the Bear found a memo from SkumTech AI about AI in the smart homes.
In the C suite, they found a few execs with their haggard lackeys meeting in a well-appointed conference room. When the Glint tried to send the sound from the remote meeting mics to his cell phone, he accidentally reversed it, sending his phone’s mic sound into the meeting room’s speakers at full blast. The heroes were spotted. An exec called security. The heroes fled, but not before Blink Lightning stole an exec’s laptop.
They found the lobby locked down, but escaped through air vents.

Rajesh returns


Abed spotted breaking news on a downtown building’s screen: Rajesh emerging from the interdimensional rift above Willis Tower and descending on Millennium Park and the Bean. Blink Lightning ran the computers back to a Lightning safehouse and met the rest of the crew at the Bean.


A special AEGIS unit was erecting a high-tech containment barrier while other non-supers suited up in space-slash-hazmat suits. Tourists were being attended to by first responders and interviewed by media and AEGIS.


Blink Lightning scouted out the area being fenced in and found Rajesh staring at his reflection in the Bean. The heroes came in, before the fence was completed and the Glint talked with Rajesh.
“Creator, I’m glad you’re here,” Rajesh said.
“Why are you here?”
“I was lonely on the other side.”
“Is it empty?”
“It is now.”
“What are you doing here?”
“Creating.” Rajesh reached into the Bean and pulled his reflection out. “Aren’t you proud of me?”
The misshapen copy of Rajesh then turned to the Bean and pulled another reflection out of the Bean, as Original Rajesh did the same. The Glint said, “Why are you doing this?”
“It is pleasurable to create.” Then four Rajeshes became eight.
“Stop,” the Glint demanded. Eight became 16. The Glint put an arm around Original Rajesh’s shoulder and tried to guide him gently away from the Bean, but Rajesh stood firm. Then the Glint forced him.
Rajesh looked at the Glint, confused. “You created me and I am creating. Why aren’t you proud of me?”
The Glint turned the Bean matte black. A deep, light absorbing black. He said, “Stop this or I will uncreate you.”


back from whence they came

Something in Rajesh broke, his face twisting. He struck the Glint with a swift open-palmed blow to the chest. The Glint took the full force of it and lost control of himself, exploding like a bomb. The rest of the team took powerful blows. Blink shielded Clarke. The fight was on.
El Luchador threw a copy into the Bean, and the Glint channeled power to trap the copy within. Another copy with enlongated arms wrapped el Luchador up. Clark cowed roughly half of them with ferocious bear stuff and the team started dispatching them back into the Bean.
Teammates lashed out at teammates, provoking rash action. Clarke cracked the Bean. Rajesh erupted, destroying the remaining copies and sending a shockwave into the heroes. Blink lost control of himself and sent a tornado careening into downtown. El Luchador lost control and destroyed a node of the containment fence. The Glint lost consciousness, and Blink pulled him to safety.
As Rajesh prepared to flee, el Luchador rashly threw himself between him and freedom. Blink and Clarke helped. Working together as a team, they barely held Rajesh. Until the space-slash-hazmat suited team came from one side and Planetar descended from the other. 

fin

Clarke sacrificed himself to protect the Bean when el Luchador lashed out at it in anger.
Miles comforted a guilty Abed: “You did your best. You tried to fix your mistake. That’s all you can do.”
Abed melted into the softest, fuzziest Care Bear hug from Clarke.

Masks: Heartland Justice, 2025-03-13
opening panels

Espinoza, the AEGIS HQ building engineer, making a call. Behind him, the steel tank holding the black tar that possessed Void is terribly corroded.
Abed, in the woods, checks his phone. He has a half dozen missed calls from Espinoza. In each successive voicemail, he grows more panicked about the state of the tank.
A janitor mopping under the tank. A drip lands on his shoulder. He looks up. A black splotch lands between his eyes.
Patton speaking at a rally at Buckingham Fountain, claiming to have evidence that elements within AEGIS plan to interfere with the election in a couple days
Miles pausing at the plaza at AEGIS HQ. Agents and supers are holding back  protestors wearing Patton masks and hats. A commander gets word that Patton’s speech ended at the fountain and the crowd is moving north toward HQ.

Dark Storm
Miles go to AEGIS Command Center to find his mother, Storm. The door is blocked, but he can open it: the body of the janitor, with inky stains on his uniform. In the center of the room, Storm faces away from Miles, heaving for air, beneath her, Planetar is laying in a pool of golden liquid. Dead. Storm turns to Miles, her eyes are utterly black.
“Why?” Miles asks.
“He interfered,” answers Storm, in a voice not her own.
“With what?”
“Me.”
She steps over to a computer terminal and types something. A moment later, Richard Roberts, chief PDG legal council, walks in from another door with an entourage of AEGIS Legal. He hands a folio to Storm. She signs. He flips pages. She signs again. Pages. Signs.
As she hands the folio back to Roberts, Miles tries to take it. But Storm and Miles both have it. Still holding onto the folio, she unleashes a barrage of blindingly fast punches, but Miles dodges them.
Behind Miles, Roberts, annoyed, says, “You know we can just print another one.”
“I want to read it,” Miles answers.
Then Miles pulls Storm outside and onto the lake. At superspeed they run on the surface of the water, but each struggling to direct the other, they trace a looping, drunken path. A cloud of mist rises around them.
Miles takes a blow and fights through the pain. He tries to bearhug Storm and sink them both but can’t. Storm delivers another blow and wrenches free. She starts running circles around Miles, creating a whirlpool beneath him and a tornado above. Miles sinks. He starts to drown.
out of the woods
After leaving Rayburn at Loyola Hospital, Abed, Clarke, and Diego go to AEGIS HQ. With his super senses, Clarke sees:

to the left: at the plaza where the protest is happening, Randy Roberts and Legal emerge from HQ, confer with a commander, and AEGIS agents begin standing down, protesters begin to fill the plaza
to the right: the march from the fountain nears HQ and scattered among the marchers are others in SkumTech exoskeletons
forward: on the lake, the mist parts for a moment, Miles sinks beneath the water

Clarke and Diego push past protestors in the plaza to enter HQ and find the tank. Abed, meanwhile, goes to the lake to help Miles.
Clarke and Diego find the tank. It has a large whole in it and is empty. They go to Espinoza’s office and find him laid out, half in and half out of his office. He’s unconscious and bleeding from a head wound, a bloody and broken mop nearby. They summon a medical team.
timeblink
Drowning, Miles has a Moment of Truth. He runs beyond the speed of light and steps out of time, watching scenes of his recent past roll past in reverse. The fight on the lake. Storm standing over dead Planetar. Calling Storm from the van.
Miles steps back into time but in AEGIS HQ, at the doorway into the Command Center. The janitor has his hand on the knob. Inside, Miles can hear his mom’s phone ring. The special ringtone that means it’s a call from him.
Miles collides with the janitor. They crash through a window. They’re falling to the street below.
double consciousness
Abed hovers over the lake. Over the cloud of mist. Suddenly, it’s gone. Actually, it was never there. But Abed remembers it. It feels to him like what it feels like when he edits reality, and he and he alone remembers what now never happened. Something changed.
Abed reaches out with his awareness and makes a psychic connection with Miles0. Through Miles0’s eyes, Abed sees him step through time, collide with the janitor, and crash through the window.
Abed goes there, where 15 minutes ago, Miles0 was falling with the janitor.
medical responds
A pair of medical first responders meet Clarke and Diego at Espinoza’s office, administer aid, and assure them that he’ll be okay. Clarke and Diego go to the security center of the Containment Unit.
They do this remembering when they entered HQ. The plaza was clear. Roberts and Legal had not come down. The commander had not ordered agents protecting the plaza to stand down. They have no memory of any contrary events.
Outside the security center, they find two security agents unconscious in the hallway. Inside, they scan security camera footage. In the shadowy corner of one camera’s view, they see the tank breeched and the janitor infected. They trace the janitor’s movements across cameras, through the building. They access security logs. They piece together a timeline.
After infection, security agents respond. The janitor dispatches them. Then the janitor attacks Espinoza. Then the janitor goes to the Command Center. Miles0 collides with him and they crash through a window.
Clarke and Diego rush up to the Command Center.
dirty window
Miles0 creates a cushion of air for him and the janitor to land on, but as he does, the janitor reaches up and places a hand on Miles0’s face. Rivulets of black tar move under the janitor’s skin, into Miles0’s pores. Miles0 sees black fingers closing across his vision.
Miles0 vibrates through the plate glass of a nearby coffee shop’s window. He stands in the middle of the coffee shop. Patrons stare at him, lattes perched at their lips. Behind him, black tar slides down the outside of the window.
temporary containment
Abed lands beside the janitor, who is just then pushing himself up on his elbows. He’s in the middle of the empty street, blocked off because of the protest to the south. He’s unharmed but for bloody knuckles. He is utterly confused.
“What the hell is going on?” he asks. Abed explains, then tells him to find his supervisor, file for workers’ comp, and take the rest of the day off. He does.
Then Abed turns to the puddle of black tar on the sidewalk. It churns. A shoulder of tar emerges and collapses back into the puddle. A hand of tar reaches up along the glass of the window and falls back. It keeps trying but cannot hold a form.
Abed reshapes the sidewalk into a vault to contain the tar. He knows the steel tank only held it for so long. Concrete will surely fare no better.
Miles0 pokes his head out of the coffee shop and offers Abed a drink.
redo
On the way to the Command Center, Clarke and Diego meet Miles1 also on his way there. They assume it’s the same Miles they saw crash through the window. All three enter the Command Center.
Inside, Planetar and Storm are having a heated conversation with Randy Roberts and AEGIS Legal. Supers Stupendo, Yellow Goblin, and Jai Alai stand by, supporting Roberts and Legal.
Roberts threatens legal action to bring all of AEGIS under Legal’s control. He offers a settlement that would avoid court. Planetar and Storm reject that. Roberts and Legal retreat, with the disloyal supers glaring at the loyal ones before they too leave.

Matt’s “Fallen Magic” campaign
2024-06-13 (level 2)
A Dead Douche, but Raxus’s Dead Douche
We continued by canoe down the Goldleaf River. Where the river bent north, we planned to leave the water to continue overland, east toward Bizzy Brambles and the Intrepid Hills.
But there at the bend, at a river town called Bitches Bend, we met Arvax the Douche, Raxus’s jealous associate from Doku Death Shadow days. (We first met Arvax when he demanded The Cursed’s weapon.) Arvax and his crew had embargoed the river and were searching all boats, looking for us and the Lightning Greaves. No one was in the mood to skulk around this lowlife, so we went straight for the docks, where he was peacocking astride a mongoose mount.
Arvax, his mongoose, two giant spiders, and 10 archers immediately attacked us. (Everyone rolled like babies but finally Artemis’s cannon went off.) When we killed Arvax and his archers, the beasts scattered.
Then Raxus fished Arvax’s body from the river, defiled it by scalping Arvax’s dragonborn crest, looted the two Shadow Syndicate rank markers he carried (his own, and Raxus’s first), spit acid in his dead eye, then gave him a proper, honorable burial because - as Artemis, said - Arvax might have been a douche, but he was Raxus’s douche.
Also, Endra planted Dragonsbane in Arvax’s wounds before burial. druidhumor
Finally, Raxus sent a message via shadows to Doku Death Shadow, using his old rank marker. “Arvax attacked me twice. He’s dead. Much love, Raxus.” Doku’s answer to his unspoken question - “WTF?” - will come in time, thanks to a Prince of Shadows benefit.
Arvax also carried a Brambles heirloom, their signet ring, with deeply sentimental value. How did he come to possess it? We don’t know. Who did it belong to? Bizzy Brambles. Boy is Bobby gonna be mad!

Arvax and Endra the Cursed
The soldier, Georg, was a low-level thug who told us about his crew’s camp outside of town. On the way there, we encountered Arvax - a dragonic of the Shadow Syndicate who’s been jealous of Raxus since Raxus was promoted to Doku Death Shadow’s guard and Arvax wasn’t.
Arvax demanded the magic item Endra carried, looted from The Cursed in last session’s fight. But when Endra threw it on the ground at Arvax’s feet, its cocoon of vines split open and, showing itself as a shillelagh, called to Endra. She snatched it up and took on the curse. Arvax signaled archers and had Georg killed. Then I called the archers off with an icon benefit with the Prince of Shadows - complicated! Arvax and his kobold crew attacked but we overwhelmed them easily. We let them flee, all but one dead kobold.
At Dapper Dan’s camp outside of town, we negotiated with the crew. Bobby gave leader, Lucas, papers for the crew to get work with his mom in the Intrepid Hills. Then we sailed to Queensgate on our way to find Mishra - an old associate of Keef the innkeep, who runs a safehouse in Old Town.

The Prince of Shadows wants his Lightning Greaves back.
Dapper Dan’s crew was sent from Shadowport by Richard Scrotes. They would meet him at the fountain at sunrise, then be blindfolded and taken to Nolak.

Matt’s “Fallen Magic” campaign
2024-07-16 (level 2)
Bizness Time
We came to the Brambles’ Keep in the Intrepid Hills—an earthworks wall protecting a bustling gnome village, with a stonewalled inner keep.

Built on and near ruins, it’s dotted with creepy statues of bird people. A dwarf stonemaster, nicknamed Thump, oversaw the building of a new stone wall. Workers and residents were abuzz, because the project had just unearthed an eldritch sarcophagus. We met Lucas, the former Rustler, working the project. He hoped to go to the ruins soon.
Endra met her traveling apothecary mentor, Hoggle, a rotund human man. He congratulated her and gave her healing salts from a coastal hellhole.
Mou5e and Raxus were mobbed by curious gnome children. Raxus was deeply uncomfortable. Mou5e showed off his robot tricks. One child brought a glass bottle gnome, Fizzy “the Wiz” Wizler. It wizzed blue goo.
Bobby went to check his family’s heirlooms and found that the Brambles’ signet ring—one of five rings from five founding families—was safely there. The one he carried, taken from Arvax, was in fact a copy.
Then Bizzy met us there. Her leg was still healing from her fight with Doku and his thugs on the island northwest of the keep. She didn’t know why Doku was there.
We went to the Vault. Not the lower “decoy” vault, but the high tower, on rails that could sequester it in the nearby mountain. This is where the real magic items were kept. It was projected by a lock from the Black, combination stairs, and a blood barrier.
Inside, Artemis’s wand perked up at the presence of a hammer—the Dwarf King’s thunderous Hammer of Colossus. Bizzy admitted that Bobby’s Uncle Bruce died trying to wield it. The wand gave it voice: it was there with all the rest of the iconic items when the Archmage summoned the Plane of Light. We placed the Lightning Greaves beside it, and the hammer and greaves mated magically and produced a magical sprite that asked us to give it an item to inhabit. Bobby gave it the fake signet ring. In a flash of light, it bonded with it, leaving the Brambles seal seared into the floor.
We debated the wisdom of leaving all the iconic items in one place. Mou5e feared theft and wondered if all together they’d complete the summoning of the Plane of Light. Bobby wanted to make new magic items and sell them. For now, we agreed to leave the Greaves but likely put a third item somewhere else. Mou5e pondered theological implications. We hoped Bizzy’s magical researchers would discover something about the mating rituals and offspring of the hammer and greaves.
There was an impromptu feast of wild boar and root vegetables. We stayed for two days. When we left, Bizzy rejected Endra’s apothecary pack but let Mou5e heal her. Bizzy gave Bobby a sending stone.
We left for the coast, to travel by sea to the Wake Islands. Raxus knew an enemy of Doku who would happily arrange discreet passage for us (Prince of Shadows benefit). But on the outskirts of the village, we found orcs harassing Hoggle. They wanted food. Also, they were Doku thugs. We murdered most of them and captured two, leaving them for Bizzy to imprison. The captured orcs said, “Doku is scouring the land for his former apprentice.”
Full heal up, plus incremental advance (the third at 2nd level).

In the Old Town elven tree cathedral, we participated in a ritual for kids. Then Artemis felt his wand moving. It was pointing and pulling in a direction. When he and Raxus let it lead them out of the cathedral, it pointed to a house across the street. Some 20 Rustlers were branding it. In moments, they broke down the door and dragged Mishra outside.
We attacked the Rustlers, 4 thugs and 16 goblins. But Endra was pummeled by her shillelagh’s curse, and Artemis’s magic failed him. Then a huge brass dragon bearing Richard Scrotes slammed into the cathedral and began torching it.
With a powerful blast, Urza emerged from Mishra’s house, bearing the Lightning Greaves. He announced that Artemis’s wand—a wand prepared for the Archmage that nevertheless eluded him when he wanted it most—wanted the Greaves. rpgs/Matt's-campaign/For-the-Queen.title: For the Queen
rpgs/Matt's-campaign/For-the-Queen.content:
prev | all | next
Matt’s “Fallen Magic” campaign
2024-05-23 (level 2)
For the Queen
We made our way down the Goldleaf River in our newly bought canoes, lead by Thaddaeus the river guide. A Santa Cora native, he had a telltale ouroboros bicep tattoo of a winged angelic snake, that promised Raxus he was a trustworthy follower of the Priestess. Old Town authorities had watched us leaving the city and embarking on the river. They  interfered with neither us nor the Rustlers behind us. “They were bought,” Thaddaeus said.
We followed the river southeast, deeper into the Queen’s Wood, toward a confluence where we might begin to uncurse Endra’s shillelagh, on our way to Bobbin’s family. Many never returned from seeking that magical place, Thaddaeus told us.
The river widened into a bog, filled with dead and cursed trees. A foul miasma choked us. Bobbin spotted a green crystal near the shore, the seeming source of it. He shot it with a single arrow. It disappeared. The miasma jetted into the sky, and the air was clear again. But Thaddaeus seemed to have noticed only fog, nothing more.
As we approached the confluence we sought, we found another foul fog in the river canyon. Artemis conjured light elementals to aid our search. And finding the river branch, we traveled up it, to a kind of stone garden in a cylindrical canyon - a blessed place but tainted.
Then the green crystal rose before us, and three spiders attacked. Raxus hewed one spider, and Bobbin, finally clearheaded, shattered the crystal with a glancing blow. The other two spiders, released from the crystal’s control, fled.
Then the Elf Queen arrived. She thanked us: she’d been blocked from traveling here or even being aware of this place for an age. But just now it called to her and she came. She took an interest in Artemis’s wand, saying it “matters more than the Greaves.” She warned us to keep them separate and not to store them together. She said she was seeking her own lost magic item: the Armor of Shards of Ice. All the major icons had a signature item, she told us, and the Archmage stole them to summon the Plane of Light. “Keep an eye on us,” Artemis asked her. She agreed and granted us each one uncursed magic item.
After she left, Endra thrust her shillelagh into a magical rock. And the shillelagh told her a name, the name of the person she had to kill to break the curse: Speagol, an evil follower of the Priestess.
We spent icon benefits to:

Raxus / Priestess - to find Thaddaeus the river guide
Endra - to aid with uncursing her shillelagh
Bobby / Dwarf King - didn’t write it down
Artemis / Lich King - to distract and make vulnerable the spiders

The session ended with invitations to take a full heal-up and an incremental and choose a magic item (uncursed!) and run it past our GM.

Hold the Gate
We warned Rando, the Elf Queen’s herald, about a pending zombie attack. Then we defended a gate. Mou5e danced a ritual to ward two sewer exits. We dispatched three waves: skeletons, giant zombies, and killer zombies with skeleton minions.
With her new cursed magic ring, Endra warded the gate during the skeleton wave, and Artemis blasted them with lighting. Endra’s curse spawned a tiny bone servant bitch.
The giant zombies broke through Endra’s ward. Artemis warded the gate again, but they broke through again. Then Raxus Blackheart charged through the twisted wreckage and smote their ruin beyond the wall. Filled with bloodlust, he used old Prince of Shadows magics (icon benefit) to call the rest of the undead horde unto himself.
Zombies and skeletons mobbed an exultant Raxus. Artemis raised a giant zombie to fight for him (Lich King benefit). Zombies took down Fluffy but Bobbie steadied him (icon benefit). Endra and Mou5e bickered about who was clericking better. Allies from other gates, hearing our fight and without enemies, came to behold the third wave broken by our strength.
Then a great undead horde stood at the edge of our range. But Artemis, Endra, and Mou5e unleashed mighty magicks (three icon benefits) as Bobbie and our allies watched in awe and, spent, Raxus collapsed. They will sing of us and this day also and not just the of Queen yesterday.

rpgs/Matt's-campaign/Hopewell-Hostel-hea.content:
prev | all | next
Matt’s “Fallen Magic” campaign
2024-05-02 (level 1)
Hopewell Hostel hearth
When we arrived, a ship was burning in Queensgate harbor, branded by the Rustlers, with a disemboweled dwarf strung up on the bow. The dwarf was Angus, a friend of Keef and fellow magic item curser. Akimbo, the old lady in the harbor, said the Rustlers asked Angus where the Lightning Greaves were before they killed him.
Raxus led the way to a hostel (Priestess benefit) by the Hopewell shrine, where he knew we could stay and likely learn more. The way was blessed and protected, and in this holy aura, Raxus became cheerful and generous - more like Mou5e. But at the shrine, in the presence of Sister Calcetta, he became nervous and submissive.
Bobby drew healing potions (High Druid benefit) for everyone from the spring that fed the Hopewell. Endra planted mushroom spores.
Sister Calcetta said, in Drakkenhall, Doku Death Shadow and Bizzy, Bobby’s mom, clashed and Bizzy was injured but would recover. When pressed by the Sister, Bobby declared that his current loyalty to us and duty to Keef the innkeep outweighed his desire to return to his mom.
At the hostel, we shared stories around the hearth. First among them, Raxus told a story Angus told him years ago when Raxus served at the shrine and Angus came occasionally to repent for his crimes against magic items. It was about a shillelagh Angus cursed, the juggling of flaming shillelaghs, which ended with an unexpected disappearance. A good time was had by all trading stories and enjoying the comradery.
We also learned:

the Lightning Greaves were named for the great speed they bestow upon their wearer, but they give delusions to weak wearers
the Prince of Shadows helped someone (who?) create them
Ersa might know where the Greaves are and only Mishra in Old Town knows where Ersa is
Mishra was a travelling apothecary serving the Priestess who, when the camp was disbanded, sent the sorcerers each to their own hiding spots, protected their secrets, and visited on occasion

In the morning, we left for Old Town, fairly certain the Rustler’s gang was headed there too. Along the way, we found the Queen’s Wood growing over the road, a sure sign of danger. And in fact, the four survivors of the gang who killed Angus attacked us.
During the battle, Endra was saved from certain death by the timely intervention of the Queen’s Wood itself (High Druid benefit). And Fluffy was killed but resurrected when Artemis prayed desperately to the Priestess (Lich King benefit). And so we prevailed. We tried negotiating with the deadly half orc leader after killing the other three, but he refused to surrender so Raxus smote his head from his body.
Level up to 2.
